messages:
olivia_support: FYI customer reported a massive delta between invoice and dashboard for a weekly run — invoice shows ~2.4M embedding units charged, dashboard shows ~1.1M. They use our async bulk CSV path, then a rerank step.
chris_prod: which customer / account? do we have the CSV or request IDs to repro? :thinking:
olivia_support: Account ref is ACCT-8342 (shared privately). They exported a CSV of ~35k rows, sent to /v1/embeddings:async-bulk then ran a rerank pairwise stage across filtered subsets later. They attached a small repro CSV and the support log. Pasting sanitized snippets below.
kelly_eng: paste the request headers + body (sanitized). also the async job ids if available.
olivia_support: ```
POST /v1/embeddings:async-bulk
Content-Type: application/json
{ "job_id": "job-20260301-01", "input_csv_gcs": "gs://acct-8342/uploads/2026-03-01.csv", "model": "redwood-embed-1024" }
```
olivia_support: After job complete they called rerank endpoint with pairwise=true across ~1k selected items. Their billing window shows charges that look like job_size * selection_count, not just outputs returned.
dinesh_billing: quick hypothesis: rerank pairwise accounting should bill per evaluated pair (N choose 2) only when using our pairwise rerank mode; but there was a recent change where async-bulk exports emitted internal placeholder embeddings for skipped rows and retries caused duplicates in metering ingestion. Need to check ingest dedupe logic.
meera_sre: I pulled the ingestion logs for job-20260301-01: there are 4 retry events around 03:12 UTC where the worker re-enqueued a ~15k slice due to transient Redis timeout. The enqueue id changed but payload identical. Metering pipeline currently keys dedupe by job_id+slice_index; if the retry generated a new slice_index we double-count.
kelly_eng: that would explain extra counts. also the rerank step does pairwise scoring which multiplies cost; are they using pairwise incorrectly? they expected pairwise only inside selection, not across full job.
dinesh_billing: customer message claims they only paid for outputs, not intermediate internal evaluations. We should compute expected charge: base embeddings for 35k rows (35k units), plus rerank pairs (if they ran 1k selection pairwise => ~500k pairwise evaluations). That doesn't add up to 2.4M, so duplication/retries likely responsible.
meera_sre: reproducer: I replayed a subset with a forced Redis timeout and saw ingestion increments twice for same slice id when retry created new slice token. Log excerpt:
```
[03:12:11] enqueue slice_id=job-20260301-01:slice-42:token=abc123
[03:12:21] worker timed out, retry create slice_id=job-20260301-01:slice-42:token=def456
[03:12:22] metering-ingest accepted slice token abc123
[03:12:23] metering-ingest accepted slice token def456
```
kelly_eng: filed ENG ticket ENG-1269 to normalize dedupe key to job_id + slice_hash (content-hash) so retries with new tokens don't increment counts. cc dinesh.
dinesh_billing: interim mitigation: we can run a backfill that collapses identical slices by content-hash for that billing window and apply a manual credit. Asking for a list of all affected job_ids.
olivia_support: customer is ok with a credit if we can explain cause. They want a short summary they can give to finance.
chris_prod: olivia, draft a one-paragraph explanation + credit amount estimate and I'll review. kelly, can you add ETA for ENG fix? meera, add the replay script to the incident thread.
kelly_eng: ENG estimate: hotfix to metering pipeline 48 hours, full rollout 5 days. I'll attach a patch link in ENG-1269.
metering-bot: Incident INC-8342 created from support ticket. Priority: P2. Tags: metering, billing, async-bulk, retry-dedupe.
meera_sre: replay script uploaded to internal-runbooks/gists/8342-replay.sh. I ran it with the customer's sanitized CSV and reproduced the double-counting locally. Will hand off replay traces to dinesh for credit calc.
olivia_support: thanks everyone — I'll send the customer the summary and tentative credit note once dinesh confirms numbers. :thumbsup:
